LESSON: WRITING USING STANDARD CONTRACTIONS AND SHORT FORMS. • WRITE USING CORRECT CONTRACTION PLACEMENT IN SENTENCES.

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Writing using Standard Contractions and Short Forms. • Write using correct contraction placement in sentences.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing using Standard Contractions and Short Forms. • Write using correct contraction placement in sentences., part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why are contractions and short forms used in Braille? 2. How does using contractions vs. short forms impact writing speed in Braille?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. in groups, discuss to brain out the differences between braille standard contractions and short forms and present their findings to peers for critique.

2. use digital devices with assistive technology to search from the internet and print soft media for the differences between the braille standard contractions and short forms and share with peers.

3. in pairs, discuss different ways of using braille standard contractions and short forms and exchange their written work for appraisal. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. in groups, discuss to brain out the differences between braille standard contractions and short forms and present their findings to peers for critique.
2. use digital devices with assistive technology to search from the internet and print soft media for the differences between the braille standard contractions and short forms and share with peers.
3. in pairs, discuss different ways of using braille standard contractions and short forms and exchange their written work for appraisal. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing using Standard Contractions and Short Forms. • Write using correct contraction placement in sentences. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: the learner engages with peer in discussions and group activities to share and critique

Braille work.

● Digital Literacy: the learner uses assistive technologies and digital devices to access and research Braille content online.

Values:
● Respect: the learner respectfully critiques other peers’ work.

● Integrity: the learner promotes authenticity in peer appraisal and original Braille writing.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer-to-Peer support in education: the learner collaborative promote learning methods relevant in modern education.
